method.scope: Representative primary sources that populate gaps in the seed atlas: reverse functional analysis, constructive quantum mechanics, intuitionistic gravity, finite quantum kinematics, and algebraic QFT.
method.selection: The supplement samples distinct foundational moves rather than claiming exhaustive coverage. Sources were selected when they change a different axis or give a theorem-strength calibration relevant to a repository dependency.
method.pinning: Seven openly retrievable PDF byte streams were fetched and SHA-256 hashed on 2026-08-11 without vendoring. Three publisher or bibliographic records remain metadata-only and are fail-closed below.
method.verification_boundary: Content hashes identify consulted bytes. They do not independently verify the papers, transfer their theorems to this repository, or establish survey completeness.

entries.citation: Douglas K. Brown and Stephen G. Simpson, Which set existence axioms are needed to prove the separable Hahn-Banach theorem?, Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 31 (1986), 123-144.
supported_statements: Over RCA_0, the separable Hahn-Banach theorem studied in the paper is equivalent to WKL_0.
entries.boundary: This is a reverse-mathematical result for a coded separable theorem, not the ZF choice strength of unrestricted Hahn-Banach and not proof that a concrete physics calculation invokes it.

entries.citation: A. James Humphreys and Stephen G. Simpson, Separation and Weak Konig's Lemma, Journal of Symbolic Logic 64 (1999), 268-278.
supported_statements: Over RCA_0, separation for open convex sets is equivalent to WKL_0, while separation for separably closed convex sets is equivalent to ACA_0.
The representation of a closed convex set changes the logical strength of an apparently similar separation claim.
entries.boundary: The result calibrates two precise separable Banach-space statements; it does not assign one strength to every use of geometric separation.

entries.citation: A. James Humphreys and Stephen G. Simpson, Separable Banach space theory needs strong set existence axioms, Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 348 (1996), 4231-4255.
supported_statements: Some weak-star closure existence statements for separable Banach-space duals require Pi^1_1 comprehension, so separability alone does not guarantee uniformly weak foundational strength.
entries.boundary: This does not make every theorem about a separable Banach space strong; the coded target and its representation determine the reversal.

entries.citation: Vasco Brattka, How incomputable is the separable Hahn-Banach theorem? (2008).
supported_statements: The separable Hahn-Banach theorem also admits a uniform computability analysis, connecting its reverse-mathematical WKL calibration to computable analysis.
entries.boundary: A Weihrauch or computability classification is not automatically the same relation as implication over RCA_0 or derivability in constructive set theory.

entries.citation: Douglas Bridges and Karl Svozil, Constructive Mathematics and Quantum Physics, International Journal of Theoretical Physics 39 (2000), 503-515.
supported_statements: Bishop-style constructive mathematics can isolate constructive properties of Hilbert subspaces and projections and formulate a constructive quantum-logical axiom system.
entries.boundary: The paper is an attempt at constructive quantum foundations, not a complete constructive dynamics, continuum QFT, or gravity construction.

entries.citation: Fred Richman and Douglas Bridges, A Constructive Proof of Gleason's Theorem, Journal of Functional Analysis 162 (1999), 287-312.
supported_statements: Gleason's theorem has a constructive proof after its hypotheses and conclusion are given an appropriate constructive formulation.
entries.boundary: This is a reformulation and proof of a specific probability-representation theorem; it is not a constructive derivation of all quantum mechanics.

entries.citation: Yuri B. Grinkevich, Synthetic Differential Geometry: A Way to Intuitionistic Models of General Relativity in Toposes (1996).
supported_statements: Synthetic differential geometry in a suitable topos supports intuitionistic models of Riemannian geometry and Einstein equations on formal manifolds.
entries.boundary: This is a classical-gravity reformulation route; it does not supply a constructive quantum Weyl theory or an external equivalence theorem for every classical spacetime.

entries.citation: Kathleen S. Gibbons, Matthew J. Hoffman, and William K. Wootters, Discrete phase space based on finite fields, Physical Review A 70, 062101 (2004).
supported_statements: For finite-dimensional quantum systems of prime-power dimension, finite-field phase space supports discrete Wigner functions and mutually unbiased line-associated bases.
entries.boundary: A finite kinematics for selected dimensions is not a finite replacement for continuum dynamics, Lorentzian QFT, or a convergence theorem.

entries.citation: Simon Henry, Constructive Gelfand duality for non-unital commutative C*-algebras (2014).
supported_statements: Constructive, localic Gelfand duality extends to non-unital commutative C*-algebras and locally compact locales.
entries.boundary: Commutative localic duality does not by itself construct noncommutative interacting QFT or its states and dynamics.

entries.citation: Rudolf Haag and Daniel Kastler, An Algebraic Approach to Quantum Field Theory, Journal of Mathematical Physics 5 (1964), 848-861.
supported_statements: Local quantum field theory can be axiomatized algebra-first in terms of observables and locality rather than beginning with a preferred global Hilbert-space realization.
entries.boundary: Algebra-first formulation moves but does not erase representation, state-existence, topology, infinity, or set-existence questions.

unresolved: The Brown-Simpson, Richman-Bridges, and Haag-Kastler entries are metadata-only; authoritative full text must be content-pinned before a corpus freeze.
The selection is deliberately representative and cannot support a literature-completeness claim.
No source found here performs a joint reverse-mathematical audit of a Lorentzian gauge QFT, BV-BFV complex, or Krein-Fock completion.

The reverse-mathematical strength of spectral measures, Green-hyperbolic complexes, Hadamard-state selection, microlocal renormalization, and BRST-compatible indefinite completions remains unclassified in this corpus.
Constructive quantum field theory in the established Glimm-Jaffe sense means rigorous model construction and must not be silently counted as intuitionistic or choice-free QFT.
